prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1053; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Reviewed the first notice of loss. Insured reports striking a vehicle while turning left at an intersection. Claimant vehicle was proceeding straight through on the opposing approach. Scene photos requested from the insured.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant by phone. Claimant states she was struck on the driver side and reports pain in her right knee after the impact. She is not represented by an attorney and says she has not yet sought treatment. Advised her of the claims process and asked her to keep all medical records and receipts.

Entry 3: Obtained the insured's recorded statement. Insured states the left-turn signal had changed to yellow and that he did not see the claimant's vehicle before turning. Confirmed no citations were issued at the scene. Requested the intersection's traffic camera footage, if available.

Entry 4: Claimant reports she visited an urgent care clinic and was diagnosed with a knee sprain. Requested an authorization form so the clinic records can be obtained. Claimant has not yet provided the bills. Noted the injury is currently listed as soft tissue pending imaging results.

Entry 5: Liability appears probable against the insured based on the left-turn fact pattern and the insured's own statement. Vehicle damage estimate received and under review. Injury evaluation remains open until the claimant completes follow-up care. Next step is to send the claimant a written update and confirm her preferred contact method.
